section: Social Studies · Ch46 — Ancient & Medieval India — Deep
subject: Social Studies
stem: Gautama Buddha attained enlightenment under a Bodhi tree at which present-day location?
explanation: Buddha attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya. He was born at Lumbini, gave his first sermon at Sarnath, and attained Mahaparinirvana (death) at Kushinagar — the four key Buddhist pilgrimage sites.

section: Social Studies · Ch46 — Ancient & Medieval India — Deep
subject: Social Studies
stem: The Mughal Emperor who built the Taj Mahal in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal was:
explanation: Shah Jahan commissioned the Taj Mahal (completed ~1653) as a mausoleum for Mumtaz Mahal. Akbar built Fatehpur Sikri; Aurangzeb was his son and successor, known for expansion and religious policy shifts.

section: Social Studies · Ch46 — Ancient & Medieval India — Deep
subject: Social Studies
stem: The Chola dynasty of South India, known for its powerful navy and overseas expeditions to Southeast Asia, built the famous Brihadeeswarar Temple at:
explanation: The Brihadeeswarar Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, was built by Raja Raja Chola I at Thanjavur. Hampi was the Vijayanagara capital; Madurai and Kanchipuram are associated with the Pandyas and Pallavas respectively.
